reasoning: This was close. Set B follows the user's stated stages more faithfully. It has a circular tank, a single learning predator, an explicit self-play opponent pool and a scored survival time. It also has more teaching value for RL: a tabular → DQN → CNN ladder, ablations, a corridor proof world, and REINFORCE vs PPO with a library PPO check. Set A changes the tank to a square, uses two predators, scores fish on hits per fish with respawn instead of survival time, and stops at naive co-training with no self-play pool. Set A wins on plan quality, though. Its roadmap has four milestones, each with a checkable Exit, and correct Depends cells. M1 is a real walking skeleton: an online Q-learning DQN spine and a REINFORCE-style PPO spine, with replay buffer, target net, clipping and GAE added later. Its 12 small pipelines each have a clear entry, and its layout gives each pipeline its own entry module. In Set B, M1 covers the whole Snake stage in 31 tasks, and most spines are marked 'fold: spine is the whole behavior' (a full DQN marked XS). M2 and M3 are one milestone per stage with no Exit. PL-01 is a 16-step table that lists fish, predator-prey and opponent-pool steps the entry never calls. B's brief is also stale: its 'Not doing' still says 'Designing future environments now', and its success section is Snake-only. B's architecture keeps process narration ('adopted before M1 is built', 'The teams revision ripples into M1'). A has its own defects: a stale Open questions section in pipelines.md, wrong Covers labels on a few tasks, and a statistically loose TC-17 oracle. Two chart thicken tasks also have to change curve.py without listing it in Writes. On balance, A's plan is easier to build from, and B's design fits the user's stages and RL lessons better.
